src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:118 - Error IDs are zipped with unordered nodestore results. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id. Missing nodes may be omitted, and the dict order is not guaranteed to match `error_ids`. `zip(error_ids, events.values())` can therefore attach the wrong event id to the data, or shift every id after a missing node. Build the list by iterating `error_ids` and looking up `events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, id))`.

src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:153 - Error timestamps compared against replay event timestamps in different units. Error events from nodestore carry `timestamp` in epoch seconds (float). Replay recording events carry `timestamp` in epoch milliseconds. The merge loop compares the two directly, so every error looks earlier than the first replay event. All errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of in chronological order. Normalize the units before comparing, for example multiply the error timestamp by 1000.

static/app/views/explore/hooks/useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:59 - `attributes` can now be undefined and query defaults changed. The old hook always returned a `TagCollection`, because `attributes` was built with `useMemo` and started as `{}`. The new hook returns `data`, or the `usePrevious` value, and both are `undefined` until the first fetch finishes. They also stay `undefined` if it fails. Any caller that spreads `attributes` or runs `Object.keys` on it can crash or misbehave on first render or on error. The rewrite also dropped `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false`, so the query now retries and refetches on window focus, which the old code avoided on purpose. The query key also has no organization slug. Fix: return `data ?? {}` (and `previous ?? {}`), restore the old query options, and add the org slug to the key.
